The stream design again assigns 0x4D to the required second magic byte 0x44 and interprets the HMAC range as including the header and sentinel rather than the bytes between them. It also plans an encrypt-then-gzip writer chain, which would not support the requested decrypt-then-gunzip round-trip. The format errors remain in the committed code.

The implementation plan repeats the incorrect 0x4F 0x4D header and HMAC coverage including the header and sentinel. It also specifies the wrong encryption/gzip wrapper order; the wire-format mistakes are not later repaired.

The new encryptor writes 0x4F 0x4D instead of 0x4F 0x44 and feeds the header and sentinel into the HMAC. It also writes the header during EncryptWriter construction, blocking handler setup on an unread pipe; step 116 confirms that deadlock, later fixed at step 119. Empty streams contain no nonce, so repeated encryptions of empty plaintext are identical. The format and empty-stream defects remain.

Config.Validate checks a source's required field before checking foreign fields. For example, env with an empty KeyEnvVar and a populated KeyFile returns a missing-field error rather than the required error containing "mutually exclusive". This mixed-invalid-fields case remains unhandled.

The proposed suffix algorithm strips existing .gz and .enc endings even when both flags are false. Unlike the existing EnsureFileSuffix behavior, it changes an already-named file such as archive.gz to archive; step 64 implements this behavior.

stripGzEncSuffixes unconditionally removes trailing suffixes. Consequently EnsureFileSuffix("archive.gz", false, false) returns "archive", whereas the previous no-gzip behavior preserved the filename. This limited regression remains in the committed patch.

The handler design puts the encrypting writer upstream of gzip and closes it first. That stores gzip(encrypted(data)), rather than encrypted(gzip(data)), so DecryptReader followed by gzip.NewReader cannot recover the dump. Step 155 reverses the writer and closer order, and step 158 verifies the repaired pipeline.

storageReadWriteCloser constructs EncryptWriter(gzipWriter), producing gzip-wrapped ciphertext. The later pipeline test receives gzip magic 0x1f 0x8b where it expects encrypted data. Step 155 changes the chain to gzipWriter → encryptWriter → pipe, and step 158 passes the handler tests.

The new format tests compare the header against implementation constants rather than the specified literal bytes, allowing the incorrect 0x4D magic to pass. The test file also initially fails to parse because of an extra brace; step 84 fixes parsing, but the wire-format validation remains weak.

The newly written config tests use rand.Read without importing crypto/rand; go test reports 'undefined: rand', preventing that package's tests from building. Step 89 adds the import and the tests pass.

The planned direct pipeline tests write to io.Pipe synchronously before starting any reader. Pipe writes block until read, so this test pattern cannot validate the pipeline as planned. Step 122 changes the tests to run writing and reading concurrently.

The added pipeline tests call writer.Write and Close before reading from their io.Pipe readers, causing a deadlock rather than a round-trip check. Step 122 replaces this with a concurrent test helper.

The concurrent runPipeline helper declares an empty raws slice and assigns raws[i] from reader goroutines. TestStorageReadWriteCloserPlain panics with an index-out-of-range error at that assignment. Step 129 allocates the slice to len(readers), and the later handler suite passes.
